---
title: "4. Compose a Pico"
subtitle: "Declarative capability composition under the adopted v0.1 rules."
---

## Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

- Describe **declarative composition** of capsule capabilities as the
  operation that binds each entry of a Pico's `spec.capabilities` to
  exactly one installed capsule, per the capability-identifier binding
  adopted in upstream [`memo2`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo2.md)
  §3 D3.
- Read a capability requirement and classify its version constraint as
  **caret** (`@X.Y.Z`), **exact** (`@=X.Y.Z`), or **bare** (no suffix),
  and apply the matching rule from memo2 §2 D2 — including the `0.x`
  variant — by hand.
- State the two resolution outcomes (`resolved`, `error`) and the
  three v0.1 error labels (`no-matching-provider`,
  `multiple-matching-providers`, grammar violation) that a conforming
  resolver MUST produce.
- Keep two course terms separate: **rule compilation** (what
  `bin/pico compose` does today, verified in
  [`memo24.md`](../../../../memo24.md) §2.4) and
  **capability composition / resolution** (the new operation defined
  in memo2 §4 D4).
- Explain why the Academy ships **no resolver** at v0.1 and what
  validates a Pico composition today.

## Prerequisites

- Lesson [1. Understand a Pico](../../part-1/01-introduction/index.qmd)
  and lessons 2 (Define a capsule) and 3 (Implement and test a
  capsule) of [Part 2](../index.qmd).
- A working shell and text editor; Python 3.8+ on `PATH`.
- A local clone of this repository (ships `bin/pico` and
  `definitions/pico.yaml`).
- No Kubernetes, message broker, database, AI library, or bot platform
  is required.

## Two terms, kept separate

Upstream memo2 §4 D4 fixes this terminology for the Academy and the
Pico ecosystem. Keep the two apart; they refer to different
operations in different repositories.

- **Rule compilation** — what `bin/pico compose` in this repository
  does. Input: one parsed Rule (today only `kind: greeting`). Output:
  one executable shell-script artefact. Verified in
  [`memo24.md`](../../../../memo24.md) §2.4. It does **not** read
  capsule definitions, it does **not** resolve `spec.capabilities`,
  and it does **not** check version compatibility.
- **Capability composition / resolution** — the new operation defined
  in memo2 §4 D4. Input: one Pico definition and a set of installed
  capsule definitions. Output: a resolved composition manifest that
  pins each entry of `spec.capabilities` to a specific capsule
  `metadata.name` + version. The normative semantics live in
  `open-engineering-capsules/source`; the reference command-line
  implementation lives in `open-engineering-capsule/source`
  (memo2 §1 D1, §4 D4). The Academy ships **no resolver** and will
  not fork validation (memo2 §4 D4 Consequences for the Academy).

## The capability-identifier binding (memo2 §3 D3)

A Pico says *what capability it needs* in its existing
`spec.capabilities: [string]` field (the Academy's
[`definitions/pico.yaml`](../../../../definitions/pico.yaml) requires
this field; no schema change here, see
[Lesson 1 — Understand a Pico](../../part-1/01-introduction/index.qmd#what-definitions-pico-yaml-requires-today)).
Each item is a **capability identifier** — matching the grammar
below — optionally followed by a **version constraint**.

A capsule says *what capability it provides* through its
`spec.capability` field, whose value is a single capability
identifier matching the same grammar.

Resolution walks every item of `spec.capabilities` and keeps the
installed capsules whose `spec.capability` equals the identifier **and**
whose `metadata.version` satisfies the stated constraint. The outcomes
are fixed:

- Exactly one surviving provider → `outcome: resolved`.
- Zero surviving providers → `outcome: error`, `error: no-matching-provider`.
- Two or more surviving providers → `outcome: error`,
  `error: multiple-matching-providers`. In v0.1, explicit provider
  selection is **not** available; `spec.composition` is reserved for
  v0.2 (memo2 §3 D3 §2 amendment).

### Grammar (memo2 §3 D3)

Capability identifiers are two or more dot-separated lower-case
segments:

```
^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*)+$
```

Accepted: `oe.greeting`, `github.issue.create`, `pico.state.set`.
Rejected: `Greeting` (upper-case, single segment), `oe..greeting`
(empty segment), `oe_greeting` (underscore, no dot separator).

### Version constraints (memo2 §2 D2)

| Form | Constraint | Match rule |
|---|---|---|
| `name` (bare) | `any` | Any `metadata.version` matches. |
| `name@X.Y.Z` (`X ≥ 1`) | `caret` | Same major as `X`, version ≥ `X.Y.Z`. |
| `name@0.Y.Z` | `caret` (0.x) | Same minor `Y`, patch ≥ `Z`. |
| `name@=X.Y.Z` | `exact` | `metadata.version` strictly equals `X.Y.Z`. |

Every `metadata.version` MUST itself be a valid
[SemVer 2.0.0](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) string.

## Worked resolution — the `oe.greeting` example

Upstream memo1 §3 publishes the following Pico and capsule side by
side. Here we resolve the Pico against the capsule **by hand**, using
the memo2 rules.

Pico (requires one capability):

```yaml
apiVersion: open-engineering.io/v1alpha1
kind: Pico
metadata:
  name: hello-pico
spec:
  type: greeter
  capabilities:
    - oe.greeting@0.1.0
  implementation: {}
  state: {}
  events: {}
```

Capsule (installed; provides one capability):

```yaml
apiVersion: open-engineering.io/v1alpha1
kind: Capsule
metadata:
  name: greeting
  version: 0.1.0
spec:
  capability: oe.greeting
  inputs:
    value: { type: string, required: true }
  outputs:
    greeting: { type: string }
  dependencies: []
```

Steps:

1. **Parse the requirement.** `oe.greeting@0.1.0` → identifier
   `oe.greeting`, version suffix `@0.1.0`. Per memo2 §2 D2 the leading
   `@` without `=` is a **caret** constraint.
2. **Grammar check (§3 D3).** `oe.greeting` matches the pattern — two
   segments, both start with a lower-case letter, no illegal
   character. The capsule's `spec.capability` is identical. ✔
3. **Enumerate candidate providers.** Among installed capsules,
   those whose `spec.capability` equals `oe.greeting`: one match —
   `greeting` at version `0.1.0`.
4. **Apply the version constraint (§2 D2, `0.x` rule).** For `0.x`,
   caret requires the **same minor** and **patch ≥ Z**. Requirement
   `0.1.0` → candidate `0.1.0`: same minor (`1`), patch `0 ≥ 0`. ✔
5. **Check uniqueness (§3 D3 §2 amendment).** Exactly one candidate
   survives; two or more would be
   `error: multiple-matching-providers`. ✔
6. **Emit the resolution.**

```yaml
outcome: resolved
resolution:
  - requirement: oe.greeting@0.1.0
    constraint: caret
    provider: { name: greeting, version: "0.1.0" }
```

That block is byte-equivalent to the `expected` block of the upstream
`fixtures/scenarios/resolve-greeting.yaml` fixture at pinned commit
`bf071c2c1b57` — the worked fixture under memo2 §5 follow-up (a).

## The 10 upstream scenarios

The capsule contract repository publishes a conformance fixture set
alongside the schema (memo2 §5 follow-up (a)). The
`fixtures/scenarios/*.yaml` subset — ten files — covers every outcome
and every v0.1 clause this lesson teaches. Each scenario is
self-describing: a Pico's `spec.capabilities`, a set of installed
providers (minimal shape), and the `expected` outcome a conforming
resolver MUST produce.

The table below lists every scenario, its expected outcome, and the
memo2 clause it exercises. All ten are fetched into the lab's
untracked `build/upstream/fixtures/scenarios/` directory by the lab's
`solution/fetch-upstream.sh`.

| Scenario file | Expected outcome | Error label (if any) | Clause exercised |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bare-match-any.yaml` | `resolved` | — | §2 D2 bare → `any` version |
| `caret-match.yaml` | `resolved` | — | §2 D2 caret, `≥1.0` same major, version ≥ requested |
| `caret-nomatch-major.yaml` | `error` | `no-matching-provider` | §2 D2 caret, no cross-major |
| `duplicate-provider.yaml` | `error` | `multiple-matching-providers` | §3 D3 >1 provider = error (v0.1) |
| `exact-match.yaml` | `resolved` | — | §2 D2 `@=` strict equality |
| `exact-nomatch-patch.yaml` | `error` | `no-matching-provider` | §2 D2 `@=` rejects even a patch bump |
| `missing-provider.yaml` | `error` | `no-matching-provider` | §1 D1 / §3 D3 no provider = error |
| `resolve-greeting.yaml` | `resolved` | — | §4 D4 worked fixture (memo1 §3) |
| `zerox-different-minor-nomatch.yaml` | `error` | `no-matching-provider` | §2 D2 `0.x` caret, no cross-minor |
| `zerox-same-minor-match.yaml` | `resolved` | — | §2 D2 `0.x` caret, same minor + patch ≥ requested |

The lesson's [exercise](exercise.qmd) hand-resolves four of the ten
scenarios and compares each result against the fixture's `expected`
block.

## What validates this today

Three claims — and three only — can be checked in the Academy today.
Everything else waits on memo2 §5 follow-up (b).

- **Capsule schema validation — yes.** The lab's Step 3 runs
  `jsonschema.validate(...)` against the normative
  `capsule.schema.json` fetched from `open-engineering-capsules/source`
  at commit `bf071c2c1b57` (see
  [`labs/greeting-capsule/walkthrough.qmd`](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/walkthrough.qmd#step-3-validate-it-against-the-upstream-schema)).
  Valid fixtures validate; the shipped invalid fixture is rejected
  with the stated memo1 §1 message.
- **Pico-definition validation — yes, via the repository's existing
  means.** The lab's Step 6 extracts `spec.schema` from
  [`definitions/pico.yaml`](../../../../definitions/pico.yaml) and
  runs JSON Schema 2020-12 validation on `solution/pico.yaml` with
  `python3 -c '...jsonschema.validate(...)'`. No dedicated Pico
  validator CLI exists in this repository and none is added here; this
  is the Pico-shape check the repository already supports.
- **Capability composition / resolution — by hand, until follow-up
  (b) ships.** The reference resolver belongs to
  `open-engineering-capsule/source` (memo2 §1 D1, §4 D4) under memo2
  §5 follow-up (b), which has not been published yet. The Academy
  therefore resolves `spec.capabilities` by hand against each
  installed capsule, in the shape of the upstream scenarios. **No
  Academy resolver exists and none will be added by this lesson.**
  When follow-up (b) ships, the Academy MAY add a thin delegating
  `pico resolve` wrapper that calls the reference implementation;
  this lesson will link to it rather than fork validation.

## What this lesson does *not* ask you to do

- **Author or ship any resolver.** No Academy resolver — not even as
  a snippet. Resolution is done by hand in the exercise and in
  [`labs/greeting-capsule/`](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/) steps
  6–7, in the shape of the upstream scenarios.
- **Modify `definitions/pico.yaml`.** The capability-identifier
  binding (memo2 §3 D3 §2 amendment) requires no schema change on the
  Pico side; `spec.capabilities: [string]` is already present.
- **Introduce a `spec.composition` block.** It is reserved for v0.2
  and owned upstream; v0.1 Picos SHOULD NOT declare it (memo2 §3 D3
  §2 amendment).
